title: High-throughput quantitative analysis of isoprenol using Agilent RapidFire-QqQ system
author: Yan Chen

steps.title: Centrifuge test samples
steps.instruction: Transfer at least 300 µL of each test sample to the wells of a 96‑deep‑well plate, centrifuge at 3,200 rcf, 4 °C for 30 min (time may be reduced with higher force); alternatively filter using an Agilent Captiva EMR‑Lipid plate (Part 5190‑1001).

steps.title: Prepare internal standard stock
steps.instruction: Prepare an internal standard (IS) stock of Cis‑3‑Hexenyl Acetate (CAS 3681‑71‑8) in methanol at a concentration of 10 mM.

steps.title: Prepare general diluent solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a general diluent solution containing 50 µM internal standard in 5 % (v/v) methanol; this solution will be used for sample dilution and for preparing calibration‑standard diluent.

steps.title: Prepare sample matrix
steps.instruction: Prepare a sample matrix that contains all components of a typical sample except isoprenol (e.g., microbial fermentation broth, dodecane overlay, or extracted intracellular lysate).

steps.title: Prepare calibration standard diluent
steps.instruction: Make the calibration‑standard diluent by spiking the same volume ratio of the sample matrix into the general diluent solution prepared in step 3.

steps.title: Prepare IP stock and highest standard
steps.instruction: Dissolve isoprenol (IP) to create a 100 mM stock solution in methanol; dilute this stock with the calibration‑standard diluent to obtain the highest‑concentration calibration standard at 11.6 mM (430 mg L⁻¹).

steps.title: Generate serial dilution series
steps.instruction: Perform a serial dilution of the 11.6 mM standard in calibration‑standard diluent using a 2‑fold dilution factor to produce the calibration range; prepare at least 50 µL of each standard and leave one well with diluent alone as a blank.

steps.title: Condition RapidFire pumps
steps.instruction: Purge pumps 1, 2, 3 at 5 mL min⁻¹ and pump 4 at 10 RPM for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Verify pump back pressure
steps.instruction: Monitor the back‑pressure of pumps 1‑4 until they stabilize within the expected ranges (e.g., Pump 1 ≈ 4.06‑4.15 MPa, Pump 2 ≈ 0.67‑0.72 MPa, Pump 3 ≈ 1.55‑1.70 MPa, Pump 4 ≈ 0.72‑0.74 MPa during aspirate/load and 0.72‑0.79 MPa during elute). Ensure pressures remain stable before starting the run; service pumps if pressures exceed normal ranges.

steps.title: Transfer 50 µL test sample to PCR plate
steps.instruction: Using an automated liquid handler, transfer 50 µL of each test sample from the 96‑deep‑well plate into the Bio‑Rad 96‑well PCR plate that already contains the general diluent solution (see step 3).

steps.title: Add diluent to sample wells
steps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL of the general diluent (5 % MeOH with internal standard) to the wells designated for samples; leave wells for blank, QC, calibration standards, and controls empty.

steps.title: Fill blanks, QC, standards, seal plate
steps.instruction: Manually add the prepared blank, QC, calibration‑standard, and control solutions to their designated wells, seal the plate with an LC‑compatible non‑adhesive aluminum seal, and store at –20 °C if the plate will not be processed immediately.

steps.title: Create plate map and run template
steps.instruction: Generate a plate map that defines the RapidFire injection sequence for the 96‑well plate; create and save a Run Template file containing the injection sequence, RapidFire method, cartridge choice, and MS method.

steps.title: Create batch and sample‑path files
steps.instruction: Create and save a batch file with plate barcode, well positions, sample names, sample types, assigned calibration‑standard levels, and dilution factors; also create a sample‑path file matching the analytical plate layout.

steps.title: Load batch file and start plateset
steps.instruction: In the RapidFire UI, load the saved batch file via File → Load, then click the green arrow button to initiate the plateset.

steps.title: Generate map file and import data
steps.instruction: Generate a Map File from the RapidFire UI (File → Generate Map); import the sample data by selecting the sample‑path file and the generated map file; verify the import log shows no errors, warnings, or skipped samples.

steps.title: Load plates into RapidFire stacker
steps.instruction: Place all prepared sample plates onto the RapidFire plate stacker before the run.

steps.title: Create RapidFire method
steps.instruction: Define a RapidFire method with the following cycle parameters and flow rates: Aspirate 600 ms at 5 mL min⁻¹, Load 3000 ms at 1.25 mL min⁻¹, Extra Wash 0 ms at 0.5 mL min⁻¹, Elute 5000 ms at 0.5 mL min⁻¹, Re‑equilibrate 500 ms at 1.25 mL min⁻¹; save the method.

steps.title: Install and condition C18 cartridge
steps.instruction: Install a RapidFire C18 4 µL Type C cartridge (Agilent G9205A); condition it as required and track sample counts, installing additional cartridges if the total number of injections exceeds the cartridge’s capacity.

steps.title: Create acquisition method (source parameters)
steps.instruction: In MassHunter, create an Agilent 6460 QqQ acquisition method with source settings: Gas Flow 10 L min⁻¹, Gas Temperature 300 °C, Vaporizer Temperature 300 °C, Nebulizer Pressure 30 psi, Capillary Voltage 3500 V, Corona Current 4 µA; save the method.

steps.title: Add MRM transitions
steps.instruction: Update the acquisition method with MRM transitions: Cis‑3‑Hexenyl Acetate (precursor 143.1 → product 83.2, dwell 50 ms, CE 5 V, positive polarity) and Isoprenol (precursor 69.2 → product 41.2, dwell 50 ms, CE 12 V, positive polarity); save the method.

steps.title: Convert sequence files to injection files
steps.instruction: Convert the RapidFire sequence data files into individual injection data files; ensure the “Do not convert missed sips” option is unchecked so that all injections are retained.

steps.title: Calculate sample‑diluent volumes
steps.instruction: For each sample, calculate the volumes of general diluent solution and test sample needed to make a 100 µL final volume using the predetermined dilution factor (example shown for a 2‑fold dilution); prepare the mixtures accordingly.

steps.title: Create MassHunter quantitative batch
steps.instruction: In MassHunter QqQ quantitative analysis software, create a new batch, load all individual injection data files, and if this is the first isoprenol analysis, generate a new quantitative method from the IP standard data file; alternative software such as RapidFire Integrator may also be used.

steps.title: Validate and apply quantitative method
steps.instruction: Validate the quantitative method, confirming that calibration‑standard levels and expected concentrations match those defined in the sample batch table; apply the method to analyze the batch and then save the method.

steps.title: Adjust pump flow rates for run
steps.instruction: Set pumps 1‑3 to the flow rates defined in the running RapidFire method and set pump 4 to 3 RPM; after adjustment, close the purge valves of pumps 1‑3.

steps.title: Export quantitative reports
steps.instruction: Save the completed sample batch and export quantitative reports from the batch table for downstream data processing and visualization.
